prf:categorical-mass-markov:
Proof Proof of categorical mass markov.

Proof

The chain has three steps.

Step 1 (Mass integrand = identity). By definition (mass), \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) = \lVert \int_A \circ \Psi \circ \varrho \rVert with \Psi = (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta. The unit law and the Frobenius relation give \Psi = L_u, left multiplication by u = \Psi \circ \eta. When the Frobenius form is the counit, \int_A = \varepsilon, the counit law (\varepsilon \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta = \mathrm{id}_A gives \Psi = \mathrm{id}_A, hence

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) = \Bigl\lVert \textstyle\int_A \varrho \Bigr\rVert .

The reason is the counit law. It is not the Nakayama automorphism or S^2 = \mathrm{id}: \Psi is a left multiplication, and it is the identity exactly when u = \eta.

Step 2 (Frobenius form = Markov trace = quantum trace of the multiplicative integral). Take \int_A to be the normalised Jones–Markov trace. It is realised on V^{\otimes n}, V = R^2, through Jimbo's R-matrix \check R. A braid word \ell_1 \cdots \ell_k has transports T(\sigma_a) = \check R_a and T(\sigma_a^{-1}) = \check R_a - (q - q^{-1}), acting at strands a, a+1. Its multiplicative integral is the ordered product \mathrm{Hol}(\beta) = T(\ell_1) \cdots T(\ell_k), and

  \textstyle\int_A \rho(\beta)
  \;=\; (1 + q^2)^{-n} \, \mathrm{Tr}\bigl( K^{\otimes n} \cdot \mathrm{Hol}(\beta) \bigr),
  \qquad K = \mathrm{diag}(1, q^2).

This functional is cyclic. It satisfies the positive and negative Markov moves with scalars q^3/(q^2+1) and q^{-1}/(q^2+1), and \int_A 1 = 1. The weight K is not chosen: the Markov move exists only for K = \mathrm{diag}(1, q^2) up to scale. This is Turaev's enhanced Yang–Baxter operator (\check R, K, \alpha = q^2, \beta = q).

The categorical trace of A acting on itself is not this functional. It is the regular trace, which fails the Markov property: on H_3(q) the normalised regular trace gives \mathrm{tr}(\sigma_1 \sigma_2) = h^2/6 against \mathrm{tr}(\sigma_1)^2 = h^2/4, with h = q - q^{-1}.

Step 3 (Mass = trace of cycle). Combining Steps 1 and 2:

  \mathfrak{m}_{q,\mathcal{K}}
  \;=\; \Bigl\lVert \textstyle\int_A \bigl(
    \underbrace{(\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta}_{= \,\mathrm{id}_A}
    \circ\, \varrho \bigr) \Bigr\rVert
  \;=\; \Bigl|\!\int_A\! \rho(\beta_\mathcal{K})\Bigr|
  \;=\; (1 + q^2)^{-n} \, \bigl| \mathrm{Tr}\bigl( K^{\otimes n} \cdot \mathrm{Hol}(\beta_\mathcal{K}) \bigr) \bigr| .

Scope. Steps 1 and 2 are proved over a generic commutative ring, building on the cyclicity, peel and normalisation properties of the Markov trace. The descent to braid classes is proved: on the tower of Artin braid groups the framing-corrected trace is invariant under conjugation and both stabilisations, every braid is spelled by a word, and the identity of Step 2 holds on braid classes. Three points are not proved here.

  1. Which algebra carries the Frobenius structure. At z = q^3/(q^2+1) the Ocneanu weights vanish on every three-row shape. So the pairing (x, y) \mapsto \int_A xy is degenerate on H_n(q) for n \ge 3, and (H_n(q), \int_A) is not a Frobenius algebra. The Frobenius object is the quotient by the radical of this pairing, H_n(q)/\mathrm{rad}. On it the form is non-degenerate for q > 1, because the surviving two-row weights y_{(n-k,k)} = [n-2k+1]_q/[2]_q^{\,n} are strictly positive. Positivity holds for the sesquilinear form (x, y) \mapsto \int_A x\,y^{*}, with * the conjugate-linear anti-involution fixing each \sigma_i; the bilinear form itself is indefinite. That this quotient is the Temperley–Lieb algebra \mathrm{TL}_n(q) is not proved here.
  2. That the Frobenius form is the counit. This is the hypothesis of Step 1. It holds when \Delta is the coproduct induced by \int_A, and has to be checked for the Frobenius–Hopf data actually used.
  3. The continuous holonomy. \mathrm{Hol} is a finite ordered product. That the holonomy of the Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov connection along a braid equals such a product of R-matrices is the Drinfeld–Kohno theorem. For \mathfrak{sl}_2 the precise statement is Kohno's Theorems 1.2.8 and 2.2.4: the monodromy of \omega=\lambda\sum\Omega_{\alpha\beta}\,d\log(z_\alpha-z_\beta) sends \sigma_i to q^{\nu} times the Hecke generator, with q=e^{-\pi i\lambda}, and only up to conjugation by an analytic P(\lambda). The scalar q^{\nu} is a writhe factor. The conjugation leaves the plain trace unchanged. For the weighted trace, Kohno's particular P(\lambda) is not shown to preserve total weight, but a weight-preserving replacement exists, which is all the trace needs. Write H_{\mathrm{tot}} for the total weight, so that K^{\otimes n}=q^{n}q^{-H_{\mathrm{tot}}}. (i) \Omega is \mathfrak{g}-invariant, so the monodromy \theta commutes with the diagonal \mathfrak{g}-action and V^{\otimes n}=\bigoplus_j V_j\otimes M_j as \mathfrak{g}\times B_n-modules; on the R-matrix side V^{\otimes n}=\bigoplus_j V^{q}_j\otimes M^{q}_j by q-Schur–Weyl duality [jimbo1986], with the M^{q}_j irreducible and pairwise non-isomorphic for q not a root of unity. (ii) The two B_n-images are conjugate, so their commutants have the same dimension, \sum_j(2j+1)^2. On the monodromy side the commutant contains the image of U(\mathfrak{g}), \bigoplus_j\mathrm{End}(V_j)\otimes 1, of exactly that dimension, so it equals it. By the double commutant theorem the M_j are irreducible and pairwise non-isomorphic, each occurring 2j+1 times. (iii) Since P(\lambda) is a B_n-isomorphism, irreducibles with equal multiplicity correspond, and the multiplicities 2j+1 are distinct, so M_j\cong M^{q}_j via some \varphi_j. Choosing weight-preserving linear isomorphisms \psi_j:V_j\to V^{q}_j (each weight space is one-dimensional), P'=\bigoplus_j\psi_j\otimes\varphi_j intertwines the two B_n-actions and commutes with H_{\mathrm{tot}}. Hence, for generic \lambda, \mathrm{Tr}\big(K^{\otimes n}\mathrm{Hol}(\beta)\big)=q^{-\nu\,w(\beta)}\,\mathrm{Tr}\big(q^{n}q^{-H_{\mathrm{tot}}}\,\theta(\beta)\big)=q^{-\nu\,w(\beta)}\sum_j \mathrm{Tr}_{V_j}\big(q^{n}q^{-H}\big)\,\chi_{M_j}\big(\theta(\beta)\big), with w(\beta) the writhe. Check at n=2: \mathrm{Tr}(K\otimes K\,\check R)=q+q^{2}(q-q^{-1})+q^{5}=q^{3}+q^{5}, which equals the triplet-plus-singlet sum q(1+q^{2}+q^{4})-q^{-1}q^{2}. Two conventions are not fixed here: the orientation q\leftrightarrow q^{-1} between e^{-\pi i\lambda} and the Jimbo parameter, and the normalisation of \Omega, which moves the per-crossing scalar. Neither changes the argument. It needs q not a root of unity and says nothing about real q_0. This is the Drinfeld–Kohno theorem [kohno1987, drinfeld1990, kassel1995], cited, not proved. For a real level the monodromy eigenvalues lie on the unit circle, so they cannot equal the real aether value q_0 > 1 (proved). The real value is reached at the purely imaginary coupling \lambda_0=\ln q_0/(i\pi)\approx -0.0332\,i, and the theorem does hold there. Kohno's Remark 1.3.14 states that for any complex \lambda the correspondence of Theorem 1.2.8 holds when the R-matrix images \varphi(\gamma_k) of \gamma_k=(\sigma_1\cdots\sigma_{k-1})^k, 2\le k\le n, are diagonalizable, and that this holds when \varphi is completely reducible [kohno1987]. At real q_0>1, q_0 is not a root of unity, so V^{\otimes n}=\bigoplus_j V^{q}_j\otimes M^{q}_j is semisimple and \varphi(\gamma_k) acts on each isotypic block of V^{\otimes k} by a scalar (the ribbon twist), hence is diagonalizable. The intertwiner argument above uses only that q is not a root of unity, so it applies at \lambda_0 too. A numerical check at n=3 agrees: for pure braids \sigma_1^2,\sigma_2^2 and the products \sigma_1^2\sigma_2^2, \sigma_2^2\sigma_1^2, \sigma_1^2\sigma_2^{-2}, the KZ monodromy at \lambda_0 and the Jimbo R-matrix at q_0 have equal traces in every total-weight sector, up to the scalar q^{-1} per \sigma_i^2, to 10^{-15}, with the residual falling as h^4 under step refinement, and the opposite orientation q\mapsto q^{-1} fails by 0.70. So, with \mathrm{Hol} read as the Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov holonomy at \lambda_0, the identity holds at the real pin, resting on the cited Kohno theorem and remark. Two pieces are proved: the two-strand case, where the Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov transport is solved, shown unique, and its exchange operator equals q^{-1/2} times a weight-preserving conjugate of \check R(q), so that \mathrm{Tr}\big((K\otimes K)(P\,\mathrm{Hol})^k\big)=q^{-k/2}\,\mathrm{Tr}\big((K\otimes K)\check R^k\big) for all k; and the flatness of the n-point connection (KZ connection). A second, algebraic route to the \mathfrak{sl}_2 statement at every \lambda\notin\mathbb{Q} adapts Etingof–Motorin–Varchenko–Zhu. What stays open is different: whether the framework's own aether connection is this Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov connection.

rem:markov-trace-gibbs-free-energy:
Remark Binding as a free-energy difference: the Markov trace in the partition-function slot. Interpretation of the categorical mass–Markov decomposition.

The binding formula follows a thermodynamic form. Writing

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}
  \;=\;
  E_0 \,\ln\frac{\mathrm{tr}_M(W_{\text{free}})}{\mathrm{tr}_M(W_{\text{atom}})},

the model quantity is the ring element \mathrm{tr}_M(W_{\text{free}})/\mathrm{tr}_M(W_{\text{atom}}) \in \mathbb{Q}(q), and the logarithm is its comparison reading, taken after evaluation (mass identity, comparison paragraph). In that reading the Markov trace occupies the partition function slot and E_0 occupies the temperature slot. The expression defines a free-energy difference \Delta F = kT \ln(Z_1/Z_2) with kT = E_0. The thermodynamic form is a formal analogy, and is used here as one. What the sources supply is that the Markov trace is a tracial state on the Hecke tower [jones1987], whose weights at the minimal idempotents — the \hat y_\lambda below — are computed in [orellana1998]. A faithful normal tracial state has trivial modular dynamics, so it satisfies the KMS condition at \beta = 0; reading E_0 as a finite temperature therefore requires naming the dynamics whose equilibrium state this is, which the framework does not supply. The scale match \beta \sim \ln q identifies a parameter, not that dynamics. Within that analogy, energy and information appear Legendre-dual. The binding energy forms the free-energy cost of the channel reweighting imposed by confinement.

The normalized channel measure \hat y_\lambda \chi^\lambda over Wedderburn blocks supplies the information-theoretic reading of that cost. It is a reading, not a second definition of the functional, and the two are not interchangeable. For the linear-chain braid word the trace ratio factorises across the inter-nucleon bonds, so the free-energy difference above becomes a sum of one logarithm per bond, and is therefore extensive in the nucleon number. The Shannon entropy of the channel measure is instead bounded by the logarithm of the number of accessible blocks; under the level-2 Wenzl restriction only the at-most-two-row partitions of 3A carry nonzero weight, so that bound grows like \log A. A quantity bounded by \log A cannot be an extensive binding energy: at ^{56}\mathrm{Fe} the bound sits a factor of 26 below the measured binding, and the deficit widens without limit. The functional is the trace ratio; the channel entropy describes what the reweighting costs, not how much.

Two limiting statements render the information reading exact. A trace concentrated on a single one-dimensional channel has zero channel entropy and contributes zero free-energy difference. A configuration that does not oscillate between channels carries no information and no binding-scale energy.

The other prerequisite: the partition-function slot needs positive summands

This block is careful about one prerequisite of the thermodynamic reading and silent about a second. It says that reading E_0 as a finite temperature "requires naming the dynamics whose equilibrium state this is, which the framework does not supply" — correct, and the reason the analogy is flagged as formal. The second prerequisite is positivity, and it fails outright.

A partition function is a sum of positive Boltzmann factors, and that positivity is what makes F a Legendre transform — hence what makes "energy and information appear Legendre-dual" a structure rather than a picture. At z = q^3/(q^2+1) the H_2 state sum is w_+(q + d) + w_-(-q^{-1} + d), and its second summand is negative for every bond and every q > 0: positivity would need d > q^{-1} > 0, while the interface letters are d \in \{0, -h/2, d_{pn}, -h\}, all non-positive. So the required offset lies on the other side of zero from every letter the algebra has, and no real E_- satisfies e^{-E_-} = -q^{-1} + d.

The Markov trace therefore cannot occupy the partition-function slot, and the Legendre duality this block reaches for is not available — independently of the missing dynamics. The trace remains a faithful tracial state and every number computed from it stands; what fails is the thermodynamic potential structure, not the functional. That is a sharper version of this block's own conclusion, reached without appeal to the \log A entropy bound: the channel-entropy argument shows the information reading cannot size the binding, and this shows the free-energy reading cannot derive it.

The identification \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}} = E_0 \ln(\mathrm{tr}_{\text{free}}/\mathrm{tr}_{\text{atom}}) is unaffected as a definition; what it does not have is a thermodynamic derivation.
prop:atomic-mass-gb-nf:
Proposition Atomic mass as Markov trace of the Gröbner–Shirshov normal form. Scope of the categorical density \rho_K. As stated below, \rho_K is a positive scalar without an independent definition in this block alone, so the relation \mathfrak{m}(K) = m_e\,\rho_K\,|\cdot| acquires predictive content only once \rho_K is specified without reference to \mathfrak{m}(K) via the graded expansion of \rho_K.

Let (Z, N) be a neutral atom with nuclear-core Hecke word \mathcal{B}_K \in H_{n}(q), where n = 3A (three quark strands per nucleon, no electron strands) and A = Z + N. This is the electron-free core of the atomic braid \mathcal{A} \in H_{A+Z}(q), not \mathcal{A} itself. Let \mathrm{NF}_{\mathrm{GS}}(\mathcal{B}_K) \in H_n(R, q_0) denote the Gröbner–Shirshov normal form of \mathcal{B}_K in the Iwahori–Hecke algebra under the PBW Gröbner–Shirshov basis (PBW corollary). The atomic mass admits the unified categorical expression:

  \mathfrak{m}(K)
  \;=\;
  m_e \cdot \rho_K \cdot
  \bigl\lvert\!\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\mathrm{NF}_{\mathrm{GS}}(\mathcal{B}_K)\bigr)\!\bigr\rvert,

where \mathrm{tr}_M provides the canonical Jones–Markov trace (categorical mass = Markov) and \rho_K provides a positive scalar—the categorical density of the atomic braid class.

prop:hecke-branching-trace-decomposition:
Proposition Hecke branching trace decomposition: \mathrm{tr}_{V_\lambda}(\rho_\lambda(\beta_1 I \beta_2)) = \sum_{\mu,\nu} \mathrm{tr}\,A^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(I) \cdot (\rho_\mu(\beta_1) \otimes \rho_\nu(\beta_2)). Let H_{n+m}(q) act on its irreducible Hoefsmit seminormal module V_\lambda (\lambda \vdash n+m) [hoefsmit1974], [halverson_ram_1998, (2.3), Thm. 2.4]. Let I \in H_{n+m}(q) be an interface element (any product of generators bridging the index range \{n, n+1\}). For braid words \beta_1 \in H_n(q) and \beta_2 \in H_m(q) acting on the left and right H_n \otimes H_m factors respectively, the trace of \beta_1 \cdot I \cdot \beta_2 on V_\lambda admits the block decomposition:

\mathrm{tr}_{V_\lambda}\!\bigl(\rho_\lambda(\beta_1 \cdot I \cdot \beta_2)\bigr)
\;=\;
\sum_{\substack{\mu \vdash n \\ \nu \vdash m}}
\mathrm{tr}_{V_\mu \otimes V_\nu}\!
\Bigl(A^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(I)\,\cdot\,
\bigl(\rho_\mu(\beta_1) \otimes \rho_\nu(\beta_2)\bigr)\Bigr),

where A^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(I) \in \mathrm{End}(V_\mu \otimes V_\nu)^{\oplus c^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}} is the operator-valued coefficient encoding the multiplicities given by the Littlewood–Richardson coefficients c^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}, and \rho_\lambda, \rho_\mu, \rho_\nu are the Hoefsmit seminormal representations of H_\bullet(q).

Corollary (the case used downstream)

Taking \beta_1 = \beta_2 = 1 recovers the simpler sum:

\chi^\lambda(I) \;=\; \sum_{\mu, \nu} \mathrm{tr}\,A^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(I),

This form supplies the scalar-vs-operator Frobenius budget in Magnitude budget: operator-valued vs scalar approximation of A^\lambda_{\mu\nu}(I). The Pythagorean orthogonality:

\bigl\| A^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(I) - A^{\lambda,\mu,\nu}_{\mathrm{scalar}} \bigr\|_F^2
\;=\;
\bigl\| A^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(I) \bigr\|_F^2
\;-\;
\frac{\bigl|\mathrm{tr}\,A^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(I)\bigr|^2}{d_\mu \, d_\nu}

provides the standard scalar-vs-traceless decomposition of an operator under the Hilbert–Schmidt inner product. No further hypothesis remains needed.

prf:hecke-branching-trace-decomposition:
Proof Proof of hecke branching trace decomposition. By Wenzl 1988 (Theorem 1.4), H_{n+m}(q) is semisimple with Wedderburn decomposition:

H_{n+m}(q) \;\cong\; \bigoplus_{\lambda \vdash n+m} \mathrm{End}(V_\lambda)

This holds whenever q is generic. In particular, it holds for every real q > 0, which includes the aether value q_0 \approx 1.11.

The branching for the inclusion H_n(q) \otimes H_m(q) \hookrightarrow H_{n+m}(q) on irreducibles is:

\mathrm{Res}^{H_{n+m}}_{H_n \otimes H_m} V_\lambda
\;\cong\;
\bigoplus_{\substack{\mu \vdash n \\ \nu \vdash m}}
\bigl(V_\mu \boxtimes V_\nu\bigr)^{\oplus c^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}},

where c^\lambda_{\mu,\nu} are the Littlewood–Richardson coefficients. One chooses the branching isomorphism that respects the Hoefsmit seminormal basis on each V_\mu \otimes V_\nu component.

An interface element I \in H_{n+m}(q) acts on V_\lambda. Restricting to the (\mu, \nu)-isotypic component and writing the resulting endomorphism in the LR-multiplied basis defines the operator-valued matrix coefficient:

A^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(I) \;\in\; \mathrm{End}(V_\mu \otimes V_\nu)^{\oplus c^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}}.

The element \beta_1 \in H_n(q) commutes with the (\mu,\nu)-block projection. The same holds for \beta_2. Therefore, the action of \beta_1 \cdot I \cdot \beta_2 on the (\mu, \nu) isotypic component factors as:

A^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(I) \cdot \bigl(\rho_\mu(\beta_1) \otimes \rho_\nu(\beta_2)\bigr).

The trace of \rho_\lambda(\beta_1 \cdot I \cdot \beta_2) on V_\lambda is the sum of traces over the orthogonal (\mu, \nu)-isotypic components. This yields the claimed identity. ∎
rem:operator-valued-magnitude-budget:
Remark Magnitude budget: operator-valued vs scalar approximation of A^\lambda_{\mu\nu}(I). For the deuteron interface I \in H_6(q), the operator-valued branching identity (Hecke branching trace decomposition) expands \chi^\lambda(\beta_1 \cdot I \cdot \beta_2) as a sum over (\mu, \nu) blocks of traces of A^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(I) \in \mathrm{End}(V_\mu \otimes V_\nu)^{\oplus c}.

A scalar-aether ansatz approximates each A^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(I) by its best scalar multiple of the identity:

A_{\mathrm{scalar}}^{\lambda,\mu,\nu} \;:=\; \frac{\mathrm{tr} A^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(I)}{d_\mu \cdot d_\nu} \cdot \mathbf{1}_{V_\mu \otimes V_\nu}.

By the orthogonality of the scalar and traceless components under the Hilbert–Schmidt inner product, the operator-valued residual holds Frobenius norm:

\bigl\| A^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(I) - A_{\mathrm{scalar}}^{\lambda,\mu,\nu} \bigr\|_F^2 \;=\; \bigl\| A^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(I) \bigr\|_F^2 \;-\; \frac{\bigl| \mathrm{tr} A^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(I) \bigr|^2}{d_\mu \cdot d_\nu}.

Summing across all 35 (\lambda, \mu, \nu) blocks of the H_6 deuteron-interface decomposition yields:

Operator-valued residual total 3.603
Non-scalar blocks 19 / 35

The operator-valued residual magnitude exceeds the scalar approximation magnitude. Symmetric scalar aether ansätze recover less than half of the structural Frobenius content of the A^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(I) family.

This quantitative magnitude budget forces the structural conclusion. The symmetric scalar aether cannot account for the empirical Z\leftrightarrowN-asymmetric mass-formula residuals (\Delta_{\text{coupling}} +0.796 MeV; T5 −0.325 MeV). One constructs these residuals to be operator-valued at the per-Wedderburn-block level.

This section develops the constructive Markov-trace engine and its structural consequences: the low-isotope cross-check table certifying agreement between seminormal character summation and symbolic reduction, the antipode polynomial symmetry and axiomatic closed form of \mathrm{tr}_M, the recursive symbolic reducer in \mathbb{Q}(q), and the classification of trace normalizations that singles out z = q^3/(q^2+1) as the \mathfrak{sl}_2 Wenzl–Ocneanu point with framing ratio a^2 = z/z_- = q^4. prop:markov-trace-antipode-polynomial-sy:
Proposition Antipode-induced polynomial symmetry q^{20} p(1/q) = -p(q) of the proton Markov trace closed form. Let \mathcal{B}_p denote the proton braid in B_3 used in Atomic mass as Markov trace of the Gröbner–Shirshov normal form. Let

  p(q) \;=\; q^{20} + q^{18} + 2 q^{12} - 2 q^{8} - q^{2} - 1

be the numerator of the closed-form Markov trace

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_p) \;=\; \frac{p(q)}{12 \cdot q^{10}}

derived via the symbolic Hoefsmit-Wenzl seminormal reduction. Then p(q) is anti-self-reciprocal of degree 20:

  \boxed{\quad q^{20} \cdot p(1/q) \;=\; -p(q). \quad}

Equivalently, the Markov trace itself satisfies:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_p)\!\bigl(\tfrac{1}{q}\bigr) \;=\; -\mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_p)(q).

Categorical interpretation

The Iwahori-Hecke algebra H_n(q) forms a Hopf algebra with antipode S(\sigma_i) = \sigma_i^{-1}. The Hecke quadratic relation \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1}) \sigma_i + 1 implies \sigma_i^{-1} = \sigma_i - (q - q^{-1}). The antipode acts linearly on the generators with a q \leftrightarrow q^{-1} component.

The Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M provides the Frobenius integral on H_n(q) (Categorical mass as Markov trace). For Frobenius algebras with non-trivial Nakayama automorphism, the trace satisfies \mathrm{tr}(S^2(x)) = \mathrm{tr}(x). For the Hecke algebra, S^2 acts as q \leftrightarrow q^{-1} on the structural variable q while preserving the algebra structure.

The minus sign in \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_p)(1/q) = -\mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_p)(q) reflects the odd parity of the proton word \mathcal{B}_p under the antipode-induced involution. Here S(\mathcal{B}_p) constructs the reversed word with each \sigma replaced by \sigma^{-1}. The 11-crossing (odd) length contributes a parity sign. Specifically, the proton's word length \ell(\mathcal{B}_p) = 11 has odd parity.

Generalization conjecture

For any closed braid K \in B_n whose Markov trace admits a closed form \mathrm{tr}_M(K) = p_K(q) / (c_K \cdot q^{\mathrm{shift}(K)}) with \mathrm{deg}_q p_K = 2 \cdot \mathrm{shift}(K), the polynomial satisfies:

  q^{2 \mathrm{shift}(K)} \cdot p_K(1/q) \;=\; (-1)^{\ell(\mathcal{B}_K)} \cdot p_K(q),

where \ell(\mathcal{B}_K) is the parity of crossings under the Hecke-algebra antipode action. The \mathrm{shift}(K) is the GS-filtration shift exponent. It equals 18Z + 21N + 1 for atomic braids per the integer-LP closure.

This conjecture is testable via the A \geq 2 extension and via the polynomial structure of the neutron's closed form \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_n) = (\dots) / (12 q^8 \cdot (q^4 + q^2 + 1)).

References

  • [Wenzl 1988] Hecke algebras of type A_n and subfactors, Inventiones Math. 92, 349–383.
  • [Hoefsmit 1974] Representations of Hecke algebras of finite groups with BN-pairs of classical type, PhD thesis, UBC.
  • [Kassel 1995] Quantum Groups, Springer GTM 155, Ch. III (Hopf antipode + Frobenius integrals).
prf:markov-trace-antipode-polynomial-sym:
Proof Proof of markov trace antipode polynomial symmetry. One proves this by direct expansion. Substituting q \mapsto 1/q in p(q):

  p(1/q) \;=\; q^{-20} + q^{-18} + 2 q^{-12} - 2 q^{-8} - q^{-2} - 1.

Multiplying by q^{20}:

  q^{20} \cdot p(1/q) \;=\; 1 + q^{2} + 2 q^{8} - 2 q^{12} - q^{18} - q^{20}.

One compares this term by term to:

  -p(q) \;=\; -q^{20} - q^{18} - 2 q^{12} + 2 q^{8} + q^{2} + 1.

The two expressions are equal coefficient-by-coefficient. Each term flips sign under the q^{20}-shift. Each pair of exchanged degrees (0, 20), (2, 18), and (8, 12) contributes equal magnitudes with opposite signs. \square

Proposition Direct axiomatic closed form of the Markov trace for atomic-braid words in H_n(q). Let H_n(q) denote the Iwahori-Hecke algebra of type A_{n-1} with Hecke quadratic relation:

  \sigma_i^2 \;=\; h\,\sigma_i + 1, \qquad h \;=\; q - q^{-1}.

Let \mathrm{tr}_M : \bigsqcup_n H_n(q) \to \mathbb{Q}(q) be the Markov trace (Categorical mass as Markov trace). It is uniquely determined by:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1, \qquad
  \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha \sigma_n) = z \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha) \;\text{for}\; \alpha \in H_n \subset H_{n+1}, \qquad
  \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha\beta) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta\alpha),

with z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1). Then for the proton's atomic-braid word \sigma_1^7 \sigma_2^4 \in H_3(q), the Markov trace admits the closed-form expression:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1^7 \sigma_2^4)(q)
   \;=\; a_7 a_4 \, z^2 \;+\; (a_7 b_4 + b_7 a_4)\, z \;+\; b_7 b_4,

where (a_k, b_k) are the polynomials in h defined by the Hecke-power recurrence a_{k+1} = h\,a_k + b_k, b_{k+1} = a_k, a_0 = 0, b_0 = 1. Proof Proof of markov trace axiomatic closed form. Step 1: Hecke-power recurrence. One applies the Hecke quadratic relation iteratively. One sets \sigma_i^k = a_k\sigma_i + b_k with a_k, b_k \in \mathbb{Z}[h]. Multiplying by \sigma_i yields:

  \sigma_i^{k+1} = a_k\sigma_i^2 + b_k\sigma_i = a_k(h\sigma_i + 1) + b_k\sigma_i = (h a_k + b_k)\sigma_i + a_k.

Thus a_{k+1} = h a_k + b_k and b_{k+1} = a_k, with initial conditions a_0 = 0 and b_0 = 1. See Table 1 for the direct enumeration.

Step 2: Expansion of the proton word. Using the recurrence, one expands:

  \sigma_1^7 \sigma_2^4 \;=\; (a_7 \sigma_1 + b_7)(a_4 \sigma_2 + b_4)
   \;=\; a_7 a_4 \,\sigma_1\sigma_2 \;+\; a_7 b_4 \,\sigma_1 \;+\; b_7 a_4 \,\sigma_2 \;+\; b_7 b_4.

The coefficients a_k, b_k \in \mathbb{Z}[h] \subset \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}] are Laurent polynomial scalars. They commute with the basis elements of H_3(q).

Step 3: Markov-trace values on the H_3 basis. The axioms and cyclicity uniquely fix the trace on the canonical reduced-word basis \{1, \sigma_1, \sigma_2, \sigma_1\sigma_2, \sigma_2\sigma_1, \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1\} of H_3(q). See Table 2.

The last entry uses cyclicity and the Hecke quadratic only. Cyclicity gives \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_2\sigma_1\sigma_1) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_2\sigma_1^2). Substituting \sigma_1^2 = h\sigma_1 + 1 gives h\,\mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_2\sigma_1) + \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_2). By cyclicity and the Markov axiom with \alpha = \sigma_1 \in H_2, \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_2\sigma_1) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1\sigma_2) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1) = z^2, and \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_2) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(1) = z. Hence \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1) = h z^2 + z. The braid relation \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1 = \sigma_2\sigma_1\sigma_2 is consistent with this value and is not needed to obtain it.

Step 4: Linear combination. One applies \mathrm{tr}_M to the expansion in Step 2 and reads off the basis values:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1^7\sigma_2^4)
   \;=\; a_7 a_4 \cdot z^2 \;+\; a_7 b_4 \cdot z \;+\; b_7 a_4 \cdot z \;+\; b_7 b_4 \cdot 1.

This methodology is fully axiomatic. It invokes only the Hecke quadratic relation, the Markov axioms, cyclicity, and the braid relations. One does not use representation theory, Hoefsmit-Wenzl seminormal construction, or character tables. \square

Remark Methodology generalisation and the categorical-mass anchor interpretation.

Methodology generalisation

The proof transcribes verbatim to any closed braid K \in B_n whose word factors as \sigma_{i_1}^{k_1} \sigma_{i_2}^{k_2} \cdots with disjoint or commuting generator clusters. Each generator power \sigma_i^{k} reduces via the recurrence (a_k, b_k). One then reads the resulting linear combination off the H_n(q) basis. For non-disjoint clusters (e.g., neutron \sigma_1^6 \sigma_2^4 \sigma_1^{-1} with mixed signatures), the same recurrence applies after using \sigma_i^{-1} = \sigma_i - h from the Hecke quadratic.

Categorical interpretation

This proposition provides the direct categorical-mass anchor for the proton. The formula \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1^7\sigma_2^4)(q) evaluates the Frobenius integral on H_3(q) applied to the canonical atomic-braid representative of the proton's GB-filtration normal form (Atomic mass as Markov trace of the Gröbner–Shirshov normal form). The axiomatic derivation makes the construction independent of any representation-theoretic parameterisation.

The contrast with the q-Plancherel-measure trace closed form is strict. The q-Plancherel-measure trace behaves anti-self-reciprocally under q \leftrightarrow 1/q (Antipode-induced polynomial symmetry q^{20} p(1/q) = -p(q) of the proton Markov trace closed form). This Markov-trace closed form does not. The two traces constitute genuinely different categorical objects. Both expand as finite linear combinations of irreducible characters, but they carry different weights (w_\lambda Plancherel vs y_\lambda Jones-Markov).

Evaluation at q_0 and the comparison with measurement

Substituting h = q - q^{-1} and z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) into the closed form and evaluating at the aether parameter q_0 gives

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1^7 \sigma_2^4)(q_0) \;\approx\; 1.884319\,467.

The closed form is an identity in \mathbb{Q}(q), so the only approximation in this line is the decimal evaluation of q_0. The seminormal route, with Hoefsmit representations and the Markov weights y_\lambda solved from the same three axioms, reproduces this value to fourteen digits; that is the precision floor of the comparison, not a bound on the agreement.

Comparison with measurement. This is the only point where the block meets data. Dividing the CODATA ratio m_p/m_e \approx 1836.15 by the trace gives

  \rho_p^{\mathrm{CODATA}}
   \;=\; \frac{m_p / m_e}{\bigl|\mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1^7\sigma_2^4)(q_0)\bigr|}
   \;\approx\; 974.44.

\rho_p^{\mathrm{CODATA}} is read off from the measured ratio. It is a calibration record, not a prediction, and nothing in the statement or the proof depends on it.
prop:markov-trace-recursive-reducer:
Proposition Existence of a recursive symbolic Markov-trace reducer for H_n(q) with disjoint-product property. Let \beta \in B_n be any braid word. There is a terminating structural recursion on words that returns a closed-form symbolic expression for \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta) \in \mathbb{Q}(q) using only:

  • the Hecke quadratic \sigma_i^2 = h \sigma_i + 1 (with h = q - q^{-1});
  • the Markov axiom \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha \sigma_n) = z \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha) for \alpha \in H_n \subset H_{n+1}, for the Markov parameter z;
  • cyclicity \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha\beta) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta\alpha);
  • and the braid relations.

The trace it computes has the disjoint-product property. Number the generators from 1. Let \alpha be a word in \sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_{k+1} and \beta a word in \sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_m, and write \beta^{\uparrow} for \beta with every generator index raised by k+1, so that \beta^{\uparrow} uses \sigma_{k+2}, \ldots, \sigma_{k+m+1}. Then

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha \beta^{\uparrow}) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha) \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta).

The two clusters share the strand k+2.

The split form also holds: \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha \otimes \beta) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha) \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta) for \alpha \in H_k(q) on strands \{1, \ldots, k\} and \beta \in H_{n-k-1}(q) on strands \{k+2, \ldots, n\}, separated by the unused generator \sigma_{k+1}.

Correctness follows from uniqueness on positive words: any two linear functionals satisfying these axioms with the same z and h agree on every positive braid word, and since \sigma_i^{-1} = \sigma_i - h, positive words determine the trace on all of B_n. Conversely, defining the evaluator by structural recursion on positive words yields a terminating procedure that is normalised on the empty word, stable under strand addition, invariant under strand shift \sigma_a \mapsto \sigma_{a+j}, and compatible with the Hecke quadratic relation, far commutation, the braid relation, Markov stabilisation, and—by Ocneanu's induction on the strand index—cyclicity. This establishes existence of the Markov trace for arbitrary z and h, and uniqueness identifies every trace satisfying the axioms with the recursive evaluator. Shift invariance \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta^{\uparrow}) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta) is the shared-strand law with \alpha empty, from which the split disjoint-product formula follows.

The algorithm and its correctness are parametric in z: no step below evaluates the Markov parameter, so the statement holds for whatever value the Markov axiom is given. Production evaluates it at z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1). This is worth stating explicitly because the statement previously fixed z to 1/(q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2}) inside a claim that never used it, which made a convention choice look like a hypothesis of the theorem.

Proof — the algorithm

Input: braid word \beta = \sigma_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1} \cdots \sigma_{i_m}^{\varepsilon_m} with \varepsilon_j \in \{\pm 1\} and 1 \leq i_j \leq n - 1.

Step 1 (Hecke expansion). Expand \beta into the standard Iwahori-Hecke basis T_w for w \in S_n:

  \beta \;=\; \sum_{w \in S_n} c_w(q) T_w.

Step 2 (recursive basis-element trace). For each w \in S_n appearing with non-zero coefficient, compute \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w) recursively:

def tr_M(perm, n):
    if perm == identity:
        return 1
    word = canonical_reduced_word(perm)          # 0-indexed gens
    max_gen = max(word)                          # ∈ {0, …, n-2}
    if max_gen < n - 2:
        # w ∈ H_{max_gen+2} ⊂ H_n; truncate.
        return tr_M(perm[:max_gen+2], max_gen+2)
    # max_gen == n-2: peel σ_{n-2} via Markov axiom + cyclicity.
    k = rightmost position of max_gen in word
    rotated = word[k+1:] + word[:k]              # length ℓ(w) - 1
    # Reduce `rotated` back into the H_n basis (may involve
    # Hecke quadratic firings if σ_{n-2} re-appears).
    E = expand_in_hecke_basis(rotated, n)
    return z * Σ_{w' ∈ E} c_{w'} · tr_M(T_{w'}, n)

Step 3 (combine). Output \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta) = \sum_w c_w \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w).

Correctness

Termination. Each invocation of the recursive \mathrm{tr}_M call either: (i) truncates the ambient algebra (n \to \text{max\_gen} + 2 where \text{max\_gen} + 2 < n), strictly decreasing the integer n; or (ii) peels one \sigma_{n-2} from the word and recurses on basis elements w' with \ell(w') \leq \ell(\text{rotated}) = \ell(w) - 1, strictly decreasing the Coxeter length.

The lex order on (n, \ell(w)) has no infinite descending chain, so termination is guaranteed. Each basis expansion involves at most n! basis elements; no bound on the total number of evaluations is proved here. \square

Correctness. Each step is an exact equality in \mathbb{Q}(q):

  • Step 1 is exact (Hecke-quadratic expansion).
  • The truncation case (max_gen < n - 2) uses the embedding H_{n-1} \hookrightarrow H_n. This preserves \mathrm{tr}_M (the Markov axiom yields the same value regardless of ambient algebra, by stability of z).
  • The peeling case uses cyclicity to put \sigma_{n-2} at the rightmost position. The Markov axiom then contributes a z factor. The remainder \alpha \beta (with \alpha, \beta on either side of the rotated cut) need not lie in H_{n-1} if \alpha contained another \sigma_{n-2}. In that case, the basis-expansion subroutine handles the Hecke-quadratic firings exactly.

By induction on (n, \ell), the output equals \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta) in \mathbb{Q}(q). \square

Disjoint-product property

Write \beta^{\uparrow} for \beta with every generator index raised by k+1, so that \alpha uses \sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_{k+1} and \beta^{\uparrow} uses \sigma_{k+2}, \ldots. Then

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha \beta^{\uparrow}) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha) \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta).

The proof is by induction on the number m of generators of \beta, with Ocneanu's reduction inside each level. Fix \alpha and let F(\beta) be the difference of the two sides. Both sides satisfy the Hecke quadratic, braid and far-commutation relations in any context, so F does too.

  • If \beta avoids its top generator \sigma_{m}, stability lowers m on both sides, and the induction hypothesis gives F(\beta) = 0.
  • If \beta = a\,\sigma_{m}\,b uses it once, cyclicity moves b^{\uparrow} to the front, the Markov axiom strips the top letter with a factor z, and cyclicity restores \alpha (ab)^{\uparrow}. The same steps on the right side give z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(ab), and the induction hypothesis closes the case.
  • If \beta uses \sigma_m twice or more, take two consecutive occurrences \sigma_m x \sigma_m. If x avoids \sigma_{m-1}, far commutation brings the two letters together and the quadratic relation shortens the word. If x uses \sigma_{m-1} once, one braid move removes a \sigma_m. Otherwise x is first reduced one level down by the same argument.

Every function on words that satisfies the three relations and vanishes on words using the top generator at most once therefore vanishes, so F = 0. Both clusters share the strand k+2, so the closures form a connected sum.

For the split form, let \alpha \in H_k use \sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_{k-1} and let \beta_0 be \beta written on \sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_{n-k-2}. Apply the shared-strand law with k-1 in place of k to \alpha and to \beta', the word \beta_0 with every index raised by 1; then \beta'^{\uparrow} is \beta on strands \{k+2, \ldots, n\}, and the law gives \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha \otimes \beta) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(\beta'). Shift invariance gives \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta') = \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_0); it is the shared-strand law applied with \alpha the empty word, since \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1.

Which axioms the disjoint product actually needs

Scope of the right-induction step. Right-induction yields z^{\ell(\beta)} directly only when every generator in \beta occurs with multiplicity one; for general words containing repeated generators (such as \sigma_1^2, where \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1^2) = hz + 1 \neq z^2), the disjoint-product reduction alternates right-peeling with the quadratic Hecke relation \sigma_i^2 = h\sigma_i + 1.

The argument above is stated in terms of the Markov axiom and cyclicity, but it uses two further properties silently, and both are named in the correctness section: normalisation \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1, and stability under the trivial embedding — "the Markov axiom yields the same value regardless of ambient algebra". Neither follows from stripping and cyclicity.

Stripping and cyclicity alone admit a counter-model. Put \mathrm{tr}_M on H_n equal to 2^n for every word, with z = 2. Stripping holds, since 2^{n+1} = 2 \cdot 2^n; cyclicity holds because both sides ignore the word. The product law fails at k = 0, n = 2, \alpha = \beta = 1, where the left side is 4 and the right is 2^0 \cdot 2^1 = 2. So a trace that grows with the ambient index alone is not excluded by stripping and rearrangement.

Normalisation and stability are therefore part of the axiom set, but they are not enough either: if stripping, stability and cyclicity are quantified over every word, they force \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta) = z^{\ell(\beta)}, which contradicts \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1^2) = hz + 1. The axiom set therefore restricts stripping, stability and cyclicity to words of H_n and adds the Hecke quadratic, braid and far-commutation relations. From these axioms it proves \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_n^2) = hz + 1 and the product law when \beta is an ascending run \sigma_{k+1}\cdots\sigma_{k+m}, and the general product law by the reduction in the previous section.

Empirical verification

proton \sigma_1^7 \sigma_2^4 H_3 1.884319\ldots
neutron \sigma_1^6 \sigma_2^4 \sigma_1^{-1} H_3 1.464034\ldots
deuteron disjoint \sigma_1^7\sigma_2^4 \oplus \sigma_4^6\sigma_5^4\sigma_4^{-1} H_6 \mathrm{tr}_M(p)\cdot\mathrm{tr}_M(n)

The two numeric entries are evaluated at z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1). They are not nucleon mass inputs: these braid words are not the canonical nucleon words, so the values must not be used for mass predictions.

The producer additionally checks the closed forms the Markov axioms force — \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i) = z, \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1\sigma_2) = z^2, \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1^2) = hz + 1, and z^3, z^4 on the H_4 and H_5 chains — together with the disjoint-product identity above, evaluated as \mathrm{tr}_M(H_6;\sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_4\sigma_5) against \mathrm{tr}_M(H_3;\sigma_1\sigma_2)^2. All nine agree to the working precision. These are the substantive checks: each is a prediction of the axioms that the reducer reaches by an independent route (Hecke-basis expansion, then recursive descent), whereas the two table entries above have no independent reference to be checked against.

Remark Memoisation optimisation and the categorical-mass reading of the reducer.

Optimisation: memoisation on basis elements

Each S_n has n! basis elements. The recursive \mathrm{tr}_M is memoised on (w, n). For repeated atom evaluations within a single Python process (e.g., in the multi-atom witness pipeline), basis-element traces are computed once and re-used. This yields an asymptotic speed-up proportional to the duplication factor across atoms. Empirically, the cache hit rate exceeds 50% on the proton+neutron+deuteron sweep.

Categorical interpretation

The recursive reducer forms the algorithmic content of the Markov-trace existence theorem for the Iwahori-Hecke algebra. The axioms uniquely determine the trace. The algorithm constructs the unique value for any input word. This contrasts with seminormal/Hoefsmit ascent, which realises the trace via the explicit Wedderburn decomposition H_n(q) \cong \bigoplus_\lambda M_{f^\lambda}. Both routes agree on values. The axiomatic route avoids reliance on Hoefsmit matrix elements.
prop:markov-trace-hecke-functional:
Proposition The Markov trace is a linear functional on H_n(q), and the connected-sum rule. Let R be a commutative ring and z, h \in R. Let H_\infty be the Hecke tower over R: generators \sigma_0, \sigma_1, \ldots with \sigma_m^2 = h\,\sigma_m + 1, the braid relations and far commutation. Write H_m \subset H_\infty for the subalgebra generated by \sigma_0, \ldots, \sigma_{m-1}, and y^{\uparrow k} for y with every generator index raised by k. There is an R-linear map \mathrm{tr}_M : H_\infty \to R that agrees with the word trace of the recursive reducer on every positive word. It satisfies:

  1. \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1 and \mathrm{tr}_M(xy) = \mathrm{tr}_M(yx);

  2. \mathrm{tr}_M(x\,\sigma_m) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x) for x \in H_m;

  3. \mathrm{tr}_M(x\,y^{\uparrow m}) = \mathrm{tr}_M(x)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(y) for x \in H_m and any y; in particular \mathrm{tr}_M(y^{\uparrow m}) = \mathrm{tr}_M(y), and \mathrm{tr}_M(x\,y^{\uparrow (m+1)}) = \mathrm{tr}_M(x)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(y) for x \in H_m;

  4. (connected-sum rule) \mathrm{tr}_M(x\,\sigma_m\,y^{\uparrow (m+1)}) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(y) for x \in H_m and any y;

  5. for an interface letter a + b\,\sigma_m with a, b \in R,

    \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(x\,(a + b\,\sigma_m)\,y^{\uparrow (m+1)}\bigr) = (a + b z)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(y).

Let q, s \in R with s^2 = q and s h = q - 1. Then \sigma_i \mapsto s\,\sigma_i is an algebra map from H_n(q), presented with \sigma_i^2 = (q-1)\sigma_i + q, into H_\infty. Composing gives a linear trace on H_n(q) with \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i) = s z. When R is a field and q \neq 0, for every splitting of H_n(q) into matrix blocks this trace equals x \mapsto \tau(x\,\kappa) for a central element \kappa, where \tau is the canonical symmetrizing trace.

Proof

The word trace satisfies the Hecke, braid and far-commutation relations inside any two-sided context of words. Extended linearly to the free algebra, it therefore vanishes on the two-sided ideal of the defining relations and descends to H_\infty. Cyclicity passes from words to the algebra by linearity. Every element of H_m is a linear combination of words in \sigma_0, \ldots, \sigma_{m-1}, so the Markov property and the shared-strand product law of the reducer extend linearly to (2) and (3). Shift invariance is (3) with x = 1; the split form is (3) for x \in H_m \subset H_{m+1}. Then (4) is (3) applied to x\,\sigma_m \in H_{m+1}, followed by (2). For (5), expand the interface letter and apply (3) and (4).

For H_n(q), (s\sigma)^2 = q(h\sigma + 1) = (q-1)(s\sigma) + q, because q h = s(sh) = s(q-1). The braid and far-commutation relations are homogeneous, so the rescaling respects them. The knot-factor statement is the general fact that every cyclic trace on H_n(q), for q \neq 0 and a splitting into matrix blocks, equals x \mapsto \tau(x\,\kappa) for a unique central \kappa; it is applied here to the trace just constructed.

Remark on scope

Rule (5) shows that a bond made of one crossing contributes the same factor a + b z whichever two clusters it joins. On the finite algebras, the inclusion H_m(q) \to H_n(q) (\sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i) and the shift H_p(q) \to H_n(q) (\sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_{i+k}) commute with the rescaling into the tower. So the trace on H_n(q) restricts to the trace on H_m(q), and for m + 1 + p \leq n,

  \mathrm{tr}_n\bigl(x\,\sigma_m\,y^{\uparrow (m+1)}\bigr) = s z\,\mathrm{tr}_m(x)\,\mathrm{tr}_p(y), \qquad x \in H_m(q),\ y \in H_p(q).

The factor s comes from the rescaling \sigma_m \mapsto s\,\sigma_m.

Remark on normalisation

The parameter q of H_n(q) here is the one of the relation \sigma_i^2 = (q-1)\sigma_i + q, with eigenvalues q and -1. The generator \sigma_i of H_n(q) maps to s times the tower generator \sigma_i, and the tower generators satisfy (\sigma_i - Q)(\sigma_i + Q^{-1}) = 0 with Q = s, since h = s - s^{-1} when s is a unit. So the tower is the Hecke algebra in the normalisation with eigenvalues Q and -Q^{-1}, h = Q - Q^{-1} and Q^2 = q.

Remark on bond words

The same argument covers any bond word placed on its own block of generators. If x \in H_m, B \in H_k and y is arbitrary, then B^{\uparrow m} uses \sigma_m, \ldots, \sigma_{m+k-1} and shares one strand with each cluster, and

  \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(x\,B^{\uparrow m}\,y^{\uparrow (m+k)}\bigr) = \mathrm{tr}_M(x)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(B)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(y).

For B = V^3 = (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3 \in H_2, a direct computation in H_3 with \sigma_1^{-1} = \sigma_1 - h gives the factor \mathrm{tr}_M(V^3) = 1 - h^4 + h^4 z^2 - h^5 z, the Borromean trace.

The \gamma\gamma bond (\sigma_2\sigma_3^{-1})^3 = (V^3)^{\uparrow 2} between a first nucleon word x \in H_2 and a second nucleon word y^{\uparrow 3} is not of this block form: its letter \sigma_3 is also a generator of the second nucleon. For a bond B \in H_2 that overlaps the second cluster in this way,

  \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(x\,B^{\uparrow m}\,y^{\uparrow (m+1)}\bigr) = \mathrm{tr}_M(x)\,\mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(B\,y^{\uparrow 1}\bigr), \qquad x \in H_m,

and the same holds with the bond placed after y^{\uparrow (m+1)}. The bond ratio \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(x\,B^{\uparrow m}\,y^{\uparrow (m+1)}\bigr) / \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(x\,y^{\uparrow (m+1)}\bigr) = \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(B\,y^{\uparrow 1}\bigr)/\mathrm{tr}_M(y), where defined, is therefore a function of the second cluster alone.

Remark on bonds that enter both clusters

Let x, A \in H_m and let Y, C be arbitrary. A bond A\,C^{\uparrow (m+1)} that uses generators of both clusters but not \sigma_m gives

  \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(x\,Y^{\uparrow (m+1)}\,A\,C^{\uparrow (m+1)}\bigr) = \mathrm{tr}_M(xA)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(YC).

With one interface letter a + b\,\sigma_m between two such pieces, the factor a + bz appears in front. In both cases the bond ratio of a pair (x, y) is a product f(x)\,g(y), so the four ratios satisfy \mu_{pp}\,\mu_{nn} = \mu_{pn}\,\mu_{np}. When all four are positive, \mu_{pn} < 1 and \mu_{np} < 1 together with \mu_{pp} > 1 and \mu_{nn} > 1 is impossible.

Remark on the bond chain

For a chain of clusters N_0, N_1, \ldots, N_k in which a bond V^3 is placed after each cluster and overlaps the next one,

  \mathrm{tr}_M = \mathrm{tr}_M(N_0)\,\prod_{j=1}^{k} \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(V^3\,N_j^{\uparrow 1}\bigr).

The difference between the trace of the chain without bonds and the trace with bonds is therefore a polynomial in the single-cluster quantities \mathrm{tr}_M(N_j) and \mathrm{tr}_M(V^3 N_j^{\uparrow 1}).

Remark on the knot factor and trace differences

For any trace t(x) = \tau(x\kappa) and any two elements a, c, linearity gives t(a) - t(c) = \tau\bigl((a - c)\,\kappa\bigr), so a difference of traces is the pairing of a difference of elements with one knot factor. On a split element x \cdot y^{\uparrow m} the pairing with the knot factor of H_n equals the product of the pairings with the knot factors of the two smaller algebras. The functional x \mapsto t(x\,b) is paired by b\kappa, and it is a trace exactly when b\kappa is central.

Remark on two interface letters

With two interface letters u = \alpha + \beta\sigma_m and v = \gamma + \delta\sigma_m, the trace of a bond between two clusters is a sum of products of single-cluster traces plus \beta\delta times one term in which two 2-cables cross, \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(P\,Q^{\uparrow}\,\sigma_{n+1}\sigma_n\sigma_{n+2}\sigma_{n+1}\bigr). That cable term does not split into a product. When one side of the bond carries no inner interface letter, the cable term is absent and the cross-ratio identity holds again.

Remark on two bonds into one cluster

Let a be any bond and N any cluster. The trace of a^{\uparrow 1}\,(\sigma_0\,a^{\uparrow 1}\,\sigma_0^{-1})\,N^{\uparrow 2} is unchanged when \sigma_0 is replaced by \sigma_0^{-1} in the transport, and when the two bonds are exchanged.

Remark on strand reflection

Let w be a positive word in \sigma_0, \ldots, \sigma_{n-1}, and let w^{P} be the word obtained by replacing each \sigma_a with \sigma_{n-1-a}. Then \mathrm{tr}_M(w^{P}) = \mathrm{tr}_M(w). The half-twist \Delta_n satisfies \Delta_n \sigma_a = \sigma_{n-1-a} \Delta_n for a < n by the braid and far-commutation relations, and it is invertible, so w^{P} = \Delta_n w \Delta_n^{-1}, and cyclicity gives the equality. The Markov property is stated only at the top generator, but the trace still does not distinguish the two ends of the strand line.

Proposition Partition-sum form of \mathrm{tr}_M via Wenzl y_\lambda and Hoefsmit \chi^\lambda_q agrees with the canonical Markov-axiom reducer.

Partition-sum Wedderburn decomposition of the Markov trace

  \mathrm{tr}_M^{\mathrm{partition\text{-}sum}}(\mathcal{B}_K)
  \;:=\;
  \sum_{\lambda \vdash 3A} y_\lambda(q) \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{V_\lambda}\!\bigl(\rho_\lambda^q(\mathcal{B}_K)\bigr),

Significance

The partition-sum form rewrites the Markov trace via the Wedderburn–Artin decomposition H_n(q) \cong \bigoplus_\lambda M_{f^\lambda}(\mathbb{C}). The Hecke branching trace decomposition relies on this decomposition. Downstream consumers (such as binding-energy analysis via \rho_K refinement and force-carrier saturation identities) require a partition-by-partition decomposition of \mathrm{tr}_M that the recursive reducer does not directly expose.

For the recursive Markov-axiom ascent and the partition-sum Wedderburn formula to agree away from q = 1, each summand must evaluate the q-deformed Hecke character \chi^\lambda_q(\beta) rather than the classical q = 1 Murnaghan–Nakayama character \chi^\lambda_{\mathrm{MN}}(\pi(\beta)).

Two layers have to be got right, and each has a natural wrong answer:

  1. Weight layer. The weight is y_\lambda(q), the Wenzl Schur principal specialisation (Hecke branching trace decomposition), and what distinguishes it from the naive two-variable Schur function s_\lambda(q, q^{-1}) / H_q(\lambda) is the normalisation: y_\lambda divides by Z = \sum_\mu s_\mu f^\mu, fixed by \sum_\lambda y_\lambda f^\lambda = \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1, not by the hook polynomial H_q(\lambda).
  2. Character layer. The q = 1 limit of the Hecke character is not the character required here; the trace must be taken of the q-Hecke character \chi^\lambda_q(\mathcal{B}_K) = \mathrm{tr}\,\rho_\lambda^q(\mathcal{B}_K), via Hoefsmit seminormal matrices at q_0. rem:markov-z-reconciliation:
Remark Reconciliation of the Markov parameter z. Two conventions for the Markov parameter z appear in the literature and in this paper. They arise from different normalisation choices for the trace.

Convention 1 (Jones link normalisation). Producing a link invariant from the trace requires a writhe-dependent prefactor outside the trace (Jones–Markov trace); the normalisation parameter absorbed into that prefactor is

  z_{\mathrm{J}}
  \;=\;
  \frac{q - 1}{(q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2})^2}.

At q_0 \approx 1.110, this gives z_{\mathrm{J}} \approx 0.027. The trace itself does not satisfy a two-sided rule \mathrm{tr}_M(x\,\sigma_n^{\pm 1}) = c^{\pm 1}\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x) for any parameter c: the Hecke quadratic relation forces the negative stabilisation to the affine value z_{-} = z_{\mathrm{m}} - (q - q^{-1}) (see below), and requiring c\,\bigl(c - (q - q^{-1})\bigr) = 1 forces c \in \{q, -q^{-1}\}, the two degenerate one-dimensional characters.

Convention 2 (Hecke tower Markov parameter). The categorical mass formula (categorical mass as Markov trace) and all mass and binding evaluations use

  z_{\mathrm{m}}
  \;=\;
  \frac{q^3}{q^2+1}
  \;=\;
  \frac{q^2}{[2]_q},

giving z_{\mathrm{m}} \approx 0.6127 at the proton-anchored q_0.

Relation to the half-argument loop reciprocal. Writing z_{1/2} := 1/(q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}) = 1/[2]_{\sqrt q}, the writhe-prefactor scalar z_{\mathrm{J}} satisfies

  z_{\mathrm{J}}
  \;=\;
  (q - 1)\,z_{1/2}^{\,2},

whereas the Hecke Markov parameter satisfies z_{\mathrm{m}}(q) = q^2\,z_{1/2}(q^2). Convention 1 normalises the Jones polynomial as a link invariant by absorbing the writhe correction into (q-1); Convention 2 evaluates the trace directly on a single Hecke generator without a writhe prefactor, \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i) = z_{\mathrm{m}}.

The negative-crossing loop value. The stabilisation rule is one-sided. For \mathrm{tr}_M(x\,\sigma_n) = z_{\mathrm{m}}\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x), the Hecke quadratic relation \sigma_n^{-1} = \sigma_n - (q - q^{-1}) forces

  \mathrm{tr}_M(x\,\sigma_n^{-1})
  \;=\;
  z_{-}\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x),
  \qquad
  z_{-} \;:=\; z_{\mathrm{m}} - (q - q^{-1})
  \;=\; \frac{1}{q(q^2+1)}
  \;\approx\; 0.4036

at q_0 (Markov axioms). This is the value that Hecke normal-form reduction yields for \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i^{-1}); it is neither z_{\mathrm{m}} nor z_{\mathrm{m}}^{-1}.

Block weights. For any stabilisation parameter z with z_- = z - (q - q^{-1}), the Wedderburn block weights are given in closed form by the Ocneanu product

  w_\lambda
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M(p_\lambda)
  \;=\;
  \prod_{x \in \lambda}
  \frac{z\,q^{c(x)} - z_{-}\,q^{-c(x)}}{q^{h(x)} - q^{-h(x)}},

with c(x) the content and h(x) the hook length of the cell x — the Ocneanu weight formula at framing ratio a^2 = z/z_{-}, verified for every \lambda \vdash n \leq 5. The single-cell case recovers \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = (z - z_{-})/(q - q^{-1}) = 1.

Monomial framing ratio and the U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_N) Ocneanu family. Using \hbar_\times = q - q^{-1} and [2]_q^2 - \hbar_\times^2 = 4, the loop pair (z_{\mathrm{m}}, z_-) at z_{\mathrm{m}} = q^3/(q^2+1) satisfies

  z_{-} \;=\; \frac{1}{q(q^2+1)} , \qquad
  z_{\mathrm{m}}\,z_{-} \;=\; \frac{1}{[2]_q^{2}} , \qquad
  a^2 \;=\; \frac{z_{\mathrm{m}}}{z_{-}} \;=\; q^4 .

Thus the two crossing loop values multiply to the inverse square of the quantum dimension (z_{\mathrm{m}}\,z_{-} = w_{(2,1)}), and the Ocneanu framing parameter is the monomial a = q^2. When a = q^N — that is, z = q^{2N}z_- — every numerator of the Ocneanu product collapses,

  z\,q^{c} - z_{-}q^{-c} \;=\; z_{-}\bigl(q^{2N+c} - q^{-c}\bigr) \;=\; z_{-}q^{N}\bigl(q^{N+c} - q^{-(N+c)}\bigr),

so with z_{-}q^{N} = 1/[N]_q the product reduces to the hook-content formula for the U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_N) quantum dimension:

rem:phi-n-global-section:
Remark \Phi_n as the global section of the categorical mass functor. In the algebraic refactor of the magic-number / shell-closure framework, the categorical mass endomorphism \Phi_n acts globally, not locally. It is not built per-vortex and combined by tensor product. Instead \Phi_n forms the global section of the categorical mass functor over the rigid braided monoidal category \mathbf{C}, in the strict sense of monoidal-category global sections: \Phi_n \in \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A^{\otimes n}) is determined by its compatibility with the Frobenius-Hopf aether axioms across every sub-tensor-factor of A^{\otimes n}, not by an additive combination of local pieces.

Necessity of dropping locality

Local trivialisation—"screening"—provided the framework's earlier explanation of shell closure: that something local at each vortex trivialises the full-twist action. That picture carries two flaws:

  1. Anomalous ribbon flux. A non-trivial ribbon (= framing) action on \Phi_n at a non-magic level n would propagate unboundedly up the brane tower (recursive-brane-tower). Each brane level A_{n+1} = A_n \otimes \Omega^1(A_n) inherits the framing flux. Without a global cancellation mechanism, the accumulated flux at the descent limit diverges.
  2. Finite observable mass. The categorical mass identity is finite: \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) \in \mathbb{R} for every observed hadron. Finite observable mass remains incompatible with unbounded framing flux.

The only consistent reconciliation requires global topological neutrality at saturation: at n \in \mathfrak{M}, the ribbon action on \Phi_n evaluates globally to zero (in the centre-of-the-braid-group sense), not locally trivialised by some spectator structure.   \Phi_n = (\text{global section of } \mathcal{F}_{\text{mass}})_n,
\qquad
  \mathcal{F}_{\text{mass}}:
    \mathbf{C} \to \mathbf{C},
\qquad
  X \mapsto (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \circ (X \otimes -).

The functor \mathcal{F}_{\text{mass}} takes an aether object X to its mass endomorphism. The global section \Phi_n at level n provides the assignment of \mathcal{F}_{\text{mass}}(A^{\otimes n}) that respects all the aether's monoidal-functor structure simultaneously—including the central full-twist action on each A^{\otimes n}. Demanding that \Phi_n form a single global section, rather than a colimit of local pieces, enforces the aether-level constraint that the central action vanishes at saturated n.

Mass endomorphism conjecture (the open problem of finding a closed-form NF for \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}) is correspondingly reframed. The reframing constructs the magic-number ladder as a structural prediction rather than a numerical phenomenon.

This remark interprets the mass endomorphism conjecture only. It makes no new logical claim. The mathematical content resides in the saturated-shell and shell-condensation conjectures, which are themselves conditional on the algebraic refactor.

Over \mathbb{C}, the projection defect \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl((\Pi_{\text{free}}-\mathbf{1})\circ\mathcal{M}\bigr) defines a single complex observable, the complex volume \mathfrak{V}(K). Here, \Pi_{\text{free}} is the factorized projector onto unlinked constituents. One defines \mathfrak{V}(K) = E_0\,\mathrm{tr}_M\bigl((\Pi_{\text{free}}-\mathbf{1})\circ\mathcal{M}\bigr). This acts as the QOU analogue to the Neumann–Zagier complex volume \mathbb{V}(K) = \mathrm{Vol}(K) + i\,\mathrm{CS}(K).

The framework's two nuclear observables serve as the two real shadows of \mathfrak{V}. Binding energy forms the real part (\mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}} = \mathrm{Re}\mathfrak{V}). This is the bar-even, \cosh, strong channel representing stable binding. The \beta-decay Q-value forms the imaginary part (\mathfrak{Q}_\beta = \mathrm{Im}\mathfrak{V}). This is the bar-odd, \sinh, weak channel representing unstable decay.
