[murakami2006, Conjecture 2.1 and eq. (2.3), \S 2, p. 2]. For the figure-eight knot this is a theorem of Murakami and Yokota, recorded in the same section [murakami2006, \S 2, pp. 2--3]. Murakami notes that Gukov's generalization uses a different polarization: the two agree when \operatorname{Re}(u) = 0, and differ when \operatorname{Re}(u) \neq 0 by the choice of polarization [murakami2006, \S 2, p. 3]. The two \operatorname{Re}(u) terms in the formula above, which vanish on \operatorname{Re}(u) = 0, are where such a difference can appear.

What this gives here. The conjecture reads the S channel as the Chern–Simons part of the deformed complex volume of 4_1 at an aether deformation u(q_0), and its surviving necessary condition for a sign flip of S is that u(q_0) cross the diagonal |\operatorname{Re} u| = |\operatorname{Im} u| between the anchors. On that path \operatorname{Re} u \neq 0, which is exactly the region where the published volume functions depend on the polarization. The leading harmonic form used there, and the refutation of the three candidate families built on it, are therefore statements in one polarization.

What it does not supply. It has not been checked which polarization the corpus's deformed-volume series for 4_1 realises, nor whether the refutation of the three families survives the change of polarization. Murakami does not give the explicit relation between the two conventions; he defers it to later work [murakami2006, \S 2, p. 3]. Until that check is made, the sign-flip analysis should be read as conditional on the polarization as well as on the deformed-volume channel hypothesis.
rem:channel-rotation-askey-lit:
Remark The channel rotation in the Askey scheme: same eigenfunctions rotated, different measures. The bar-even (binding, \cosh) and bar-odd (\mathfrak{Q}_\beta, \sinh) channels of the complex volume \mathfrak{V} constitute a single Askey-scheme family evaluated through a rotation. Both the rotation and its limits are classical.

Channel recurrences

The continuous q-Hermite polynomials H_n(x \mid q) construct the proved basis of the binding kernel. Under simultaneous variable rotation x \mapsto ix and bar involution q \mapsto q^{-1}, they yield the Ismail–Masson q^{-1}-Hermite polynomials:

h_n(x \mid q) \;=\; i^{-n}\, H_n(ix \mid q^{-1}).

The two channel recurrences are identical up to this rotation. This is proved generically over a commutative ring R equipped with a bar involution \sigma and a formal rotation element \iota satisfying \iota^2 = -1: a sequence satisfies the odd-channel step at (q, x) if and only if its \iota-rotation satisfies the even-channel step at (\sigma q, \iota x). The archimedean i emerges only downstream of the functor \tau.

Orthogonality measures

The shared recurrence does not imply a shared spectral measure. The asymmetry remains structural:

even channel (binding) odd channel (\mathfrak{Q}_\beta)
polynomials H_n(x \mid q), x = \cos\theta h_n(x \mid q), x = \sinh t
locus compact, x \in [-1, 1] non-compact, x \in \mathbb{R}
measure q-Plancherel weight (determinate) indeterminate moment problem
at q_0 > 1 does not exist archimedeanly native regime

At the aether anchor q_0 > 1, the even channel has no Bożejko–Speicher q-Fock realisation (Bożejko–Speicher q-Gaussian obstruction at the aether q_0 > 1); its moment sequence is still positive definite, but no representing measure has a finite moment-generating function. The rotation is therefore irreducibly fibre-level, consistent with observable \mathrm{Im}(q_0) = 0. Measure asymmetry explains why parity projection left the binding error unchanged while the recurrence tie holds. A three-term recurrence is measure-independent, whereas a projection is not.

Literature precedents

  1. Askey and Ismail–Masson: The q > 1 continuation of continuous q-Hermite [askey1989qhermite] provides the eigenfunction rotation [ismail-masson1994].
  2. The modular double: The non-compact channel couples q = e^{i\pi b^2} to \tilde{q} = e^{-i\pi/b^2}. Ponsot–Teschner Racah–Wigner coefficients for U_q(\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R})) [ponsot-teschner2001] sit at the non-compact Askey–Wilson level. The map b \leftrightarrow 1/b drives the 6j-level rotation: the self-dual representations of U_q are automatically U_{\tilde q}-representations [terashima-yamazaki2013, §2.1, §2.3]. That source writes \tilde q = e^{+i\pi/b^2}, the complex conjugate of the \tilde q above. This divides \Phi_q (Faddeev, non-compact) from \mathrm{Li}_2^q (Rogers, compact).
  3. Quantum modularity: The Andersen–Kashaev state integral of a knot factors into a q-series and a \tilde{q}-series. The leading asymptotics trace \mathrm{Vol} + i\,\mathrm{CS} [garoufalidis-zagier-2024]. One complex object dictates two channel factorizations, mirroring the Neumann–Zagier structure [neumann-zagier1985] that \mathfrak{V} transports to binding and decay.

Leonard pairs

Zhedanov's AW(3) algebra [zhedanov1991] embeds the rotation as an operator identity. It pairs two operators, each tridiagonal in the other's eigenbasis, with Askey–Wilson polynomials forming the overlap matrix. The generic statement—that any eigencolumn of the channel tridiagonal operator has orthogonal-polynomial entries—is proved. The self-duality that places the channel overlap into the Askey–Wilson family via Terwilliger's classification [terwilliger2001] remains a conjectural hypothesis.

Vertex-algebra shadow

Under the bar involution, the character side splits as a \mathbb{Z}_2-orbifold V = V^+ \oplus V^-. The involved characters form false theta functions, appearing as (1,p) singlet log-VOA characters [creutzig-milas2014]. Their quantum modularity tracks the disk-interior versus root-of-unity rotation, using the Lawrence–Zagier \Psi operation established for W_\lambda. This structure suggests a path to unify the lepton-tower \Phi_q mechanism with the binding/decay model.
conj:whipple-rotation-intertwining:
Conjecture Whipple–rotation intertwining: the channel rotation acts on the toroidal family as the degree–order (winding) exchange. The archimedean shadow of the fibre-level channel rotation (x, q) \mapsto (ix, q^{-1}) acts on the toroidal channel family P^{\mu}_{\nu - 1/2}(\cosh\eta)\, e^{i\mu\theta} e^{i\nu\varphi} as the Whipple degree–order exchange: it swaps the two winding gradings (\mu, \nu) \mapsto (\nu, \mu) and is involutive on the ladder data.

Established results and open questions

The following supporting facts are verified:

  • the interpolating ladder is bar-even, [d]_{q^{-1}} = [d]_q (exact);
  • the Whipple argument exchange \cosh\eta \leftrightarrow \coth\eta is an exact involution, and the \zeta_4 quarter-period shift \cosh(t + i\pi/2) = i\sinh t maps the bar-even to the bar-odd channel;
  • numerically at 50 digits, the toroidal pair obeys
P^{-\mu}_{\nu-1/2}(\coth a)
= C(\nu, \mu)\, \sqrt{\sinh a}\;\, Q^{\nu}_{\mu-1/2}(\cosh a),

with a-independent C whose shift laws C(\nu, \mu+1)/C(\nu,\mu) = 1/(\nu+\mu+\tfrac{1}{2}) and C(\nu+1, \mu)/C(\nu,\mu) = -1/(\nu+\mu+\tfrac{1}{2}) carry a single \Gamma(\nu+\mu+\tfrac{1}{2}) with an alternating \nu-sign [whipple1917];

  • the constant's full Gamma structure is a symbolic-exact structural identity, grid-verified (not one-point): solving the two shift recurrences forces C(\nu,\mu) = \sqrt{2/\pi}\;e^{-i\pi\nu}/\Gamma(\nu+\mu+\tfrac{1}{2}), which matches the direct 60-digit compute to \sim 10^{-40} across a grid of generic non-integer, non-half-integer (\nu,\mu) points;
  • the order \mu = \tfrac{1}{2} and the half-integer degree are forced by the Hoefsmit mixing structure (prop:hoefsmit-toroidal-ladder-locus);
  • the exchange holds at the physical forced windings themselves: at (\mu, \nu) = (\tfrac{1}{2}, d - \tfrac{1}{2}) for axial distances d \in \{2, 3, 4\} (the meson is d = 2) the same \Gamma-constant identity is exact to \sim 10^{-50} — not only at the generic grid points, which deliberately avoided the \mu = \tfrac{1}{2} order — and the order-ladder factor reproduces the mixing numerator d^2 - 1 at each d. This is numerical evidence for the modeling layer, not a proof.

Open is the identification itself: that the channel rotation of the Ismail–Masson pair [ismail-masson1994] — the map carrying the bar-even recurrence to the bar-odd one — descends to the toroidal family as the Whipple exchange, i.e. that the two winding oscillations of a bound vortex pair are swapped by the aether bar involution. This is stated as a primary conjecture: the rotation swaps the two winding gradings and is involutive on ladder data. No proof is given; the conjecture is open.

Two consequences are derived from the conjecture (conditional on it):

  • the along-loop winding is restored after a double rotation, so the winding pair (\mu, \nu) is fixed by \mathrm{rot}^2 (the categorical shadow of the exact \cosh\eta \leftrightarrow \coth\eta involution);
  • the winding-grading map x \mapsto (\mu(x), \nu(x)) intertwines the channel rotation with the coordinate swap: (\mu(\mathrm{rot}\,x), \nu(\mathrm{rot}\,x)) = \mathrm{swap}(\mu(x), \nu(x)). This is the exact discrete shadow of the Whipple degree–order exchange (\mu, \nu) \mapsto (\nu, \mu), and a genuine consequence of the two swap components of the conjecture (not a restatement).

The archimedean amplitude of that exchange is fixed independently of the open identification: the grid-verified constant C(\nu,\mu) = \sqrt{2/\pi}\,e^{-i\pi\nu}/\Gamma(\nu+\mu+\tfrac{1}{2}) above is the symbolic-exact shadow the intertwining must carry.

The grading-swap component is moreover not primitive: it is derived from the even\leftrightarrowodd channel flip that prop on the channel rotation proves. A channel-indexed ladder carries the two recurrence-channel indices, the rotation that flips them, and a single shared winding function \mathrm{windOf}; the swap \mathrm{windOf}(\mathrm{evenIdx}(\mathrm{rot}\,x)) = \mathrm{windOf}(\mathrm{oddIdx}\,x) then follows from the flip, not from an assumption. This does not close the conjecture: it moves the open content off the swap and onto (i) identifying the abstract channel flip with the channel-rotation step's \mathrm{oddStep} \leftrightarrow \mathrm{evenStep} carry, and (ii) the residual involutivity — the order-2 Whipple \cosh\eta \leftrightarrow \coth\eta exchange, a different map from the order-4 \zeta_4 recurrence rotation, hence genuinely open.
rem:complex-volume-character-variety-pat:
Remark Bound \leftrightarrow free as a character-variety path: the deformation reading of \mathfrak{V}. The interpolation between the bound and free projections of Complex-volume unification constitutes a path. The bar-odd channel provides its holonomy. No structure beyond the deformation itself is required to rotate between the bound and free states.

Endpoints as representations

The free projection \Pi_{\text{free}} drops inter-constituent confining crossings, retaining only linking data. It constructs the abelian representation of the knot group. The bound object—the full braiding—constructs the discrete-faithful side. These define the two distinguished points of the character variety of K.

Path integral reading

Neumann and Zagier defined the complex volume as the integral of a holomorphic 1-form along the path in the character variety connecting these representations [neumann-zagier1985]. Transported to \mathfrak{V}:

\mathfrak{V} \;=\; \Phi(\text{bound}) - \Phi(\text{free}),
\qquad
\mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}} = \mathrm{Re}\mathfrak{V},
\quad
\mathfrak{Q}_\beta = \mathrm{Im}\mathfrak{V},

where \Phi acts as a potential on the deformation path. The endpoint difference of \Phi equals the projection defect \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl((\Pi_{\text{free}} - \mathbf{1}) \circ \mathcal{M}\bigr). Its bar-even part represents the volume (binding) channel. Its bar-odd part captures the phase accumulated along the path. This matches how the Chern–Simons invariant acts as the phase companion to hyperbolic volume, consistent with the state-integral factorization picture [garoufalidis-zagier-2024]. For the figure-eight knot this phase is extracted along a one-parameter path of irreducible \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{C}) representations, with meridian eigenvalue e^{u/2} for real 0 < u < 0.9624, from the coloured Jones asymptotics jointly with the twisted Reidemeister torsion [murakami-h2011, Thm. 1.4]; that result says nothing about the abelian endpoint of the path.

In the literature, the classical limit of a quantum-dilogarithm integral knot invariant has saddle-point equations that coincide with the hyperbolicity (gluing) consistency conditions, and evaluates to a sum of Rogers dilogarithms when the geometrically preferred solutions dominate [hikami2001, §5, eq. (5.20)]. Completeness of that saddle-point picture and the choice of branch are not proved there.

Categorical carrier

Prior to archimedean evaluation (over a generic ring R with a bar involution), the deformation parameter t of a single Askey–Wilson tridiagonal family carries the path. At t = 0, the family sits at the q-Hermite bottom of the scheme. Here, all Askey–Wilson parameters vanish, and the orthogonality measure uses the q-Plancherel weight W_\lambda, representing the free side. At t = 1, it supplies the bound channel data.

This is stated as a conjecture. It specifies the family, the q-Hermite free endpoint, the potential yielding \mathfrak{V}, and a single three-term ladder recurrence with a bar-even multiplier. The two-channel descent—where both the binding and \mathfrak{Q}_\beta ladders satisfy the exact same recurrence—is derived from the bar-involution descent of three-term recurrences, rather than assumed.

Falsifiable consequences

The class predicts one decidable numerical signature: the binding and \mathfrak{Q}_\beta channel ladders share a single bar-even three-term multiplier. Equivalently, the multiplier solved from the complex ladder \mathfrak{V}_A has a vanishing bar-odd part. This probes the holomorphic connection.

The mechanism remains computationally confirmed. The Hopf-power tower \mathfrak{V}_n = \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl((\sigma_1^2)^n\bigr) strictly follows a three-term recurrence with the bar-even multiplier q^2 + q^{-2} (the continuous q-ultraspherical class). This exercises the recurrence descent end-to-end.

The physical identification—that the measured c_k-ladder exemplifies this mechanism—remains open; it depends on the even-channel c_3. Along the isotope triples ({}^2\mathrm{H}, {}^3\mathrm{H}, {}^4\mathrm{He}) and ({}^2\mathrm{H}, {}^3\mathrm{He}, {}^4\mathrm{He}), the parity split of the log-trace binding proxy does not share one bar-even multiplier. This refutes that specific ladder construction, but leaves the underlying mechanism—confirmed at the fibre level by the Hopf tower—intact.
prop:color-spacetime-s5-factorization:
Proposition Color and spacetime are orthogonal S_2\times S_3 factors of the Bring Galois group S_5. Let K be a Bring-embeddable knot evaluated through the categorical Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M on the Hecke algebra H_2(q) \oplus H_3(q), whose 2+3=5 irreducible representations constitute the Bring fivefold, with Bring's five homogeneous coordinates split as spacetime (x_0, x_1) and color (x_2, x_3, x_4). The aether Galois group S_5 contains the block-diagonal product

  S_2 \times S_3 \hookrightarrow S_5.

Then:

  1. The factorization S_2 \times S_3 \hookrightarrow S_5 acts faithfully.
  2. The color factor S_3 fixes every spacetime coordinate. The spacetime factor S_2 fixes every color coordinate. The two sectors remain orthogonal.
  3. Every additive homomorphism from the connected phase parameter \mathbb{R} to a finite group is trivial.
rem:mass-modulus-em-phase-color-grading:
Remark Mass is the modulus, electromagnetism the phase, color the S_3 grading of one trace. The factorization of Color and spacetime are orthogonal S_2\times S_3 factors of the Bring Galois group S_5 fixes how the three observables of a Bring-embeddable knot sit on the single trace scalar \mathrm{tr}_M and its trace algebra H_2(q)\oplus H_3(q).

Three readings of one trace

One writes the trace scalar in polar form:

  \mathrm{tr}_M \;=\; \lVert\mathrm{tr}_M\rVert\,\exp\!\big(i\,\arg\mathrm{tr}_M\big).

This forms the multiplicative companion of the additive complex-volume reconstruction \mathrm{Re}\mathfrak{V}+i\mathrm{Im}\mathfrak{V}=\mathfrak{V} (Complex-volume unification). One then has:

reading quantity sector character
mass modulus \lVert\mathrm{tr}_M\rVert both nonnegative magnitude
electromagnetism argument \arg\mathrm{tr}_M spacetime / S_2 continuous U(1)
color S_3 irrep grading color / S_3 discrete

Mass evaluates the magnitude that survives both sectors. The argument evaluates the continuous U(1) framing/Chern–Simons phase. This provides the \mathrm{Im}\mathfrak{V} channel, picked up as the ribbon twist q^{2w\,c(\lambda)} on a framed knot of writhe w. The identification of this channel with a bar-odd part is conjectural (The binding trace and the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta residue are the bar-even and bar-odd parts of one fibre element). It lives in the spacetime block, where one reads it as the electromagnetic phase. Color provides the discrete grading of the algebra element across the H_3(q) representations, before the trace collapses it to a scalar.

Color is not the phase

The color factor S_3 fixes the spacetime coordinates. The spacetime factor S_2 fixes the color coordinates (Color and spacetime are orthogonal S_2\times S_3 factors of the Bring Galois group S_5, parts 1–2). Therefore, color and electromagnetism form independent coordinates. The discrete color charge is not a function of the continuous phase, and conversely. The rigidity in part 3 of that proposition makes this non-coincidence sharp. A continuous winding argument cannot factor through a finite group such as \mu_5. Thus, \arg\mathrm{tr}_M remains structurally barred from being a color character.

The two remain nonetheless faces of one aether. The Galois group S_5 properly contains S_2\times S_3. Its remaining generators carry spacetime indices into color indices. An electromagnetic-to-color relation therefore forms an S_5 statement, realized by those off-block generators, not a relation internal to the U(1) phase.

Archimedean realization

The polar split provides the archimedean reading. The modulus and argument require the realization of the trace over \mathbb{C}, on the far side of the algebraic-to-archimedean wall. The structural content of Color and spacetime are orthogonal S_2\times S_3 factors of the Bring Galois group S_5—the faithful S_2\times S_3\hookrightarrow S_5 embedding, the orthogonality of the two sectors, and the divisibility rigidity—is generic and requires no such realization.

Relation to the literature

The individual ingredients form classical results. The imaginary partner of a hyperbolic volume forms a Chern–Simons invariant (Neumann–Zagier [neumann-zagier1985]). The colored-Jones asymptotics realize this complex volume at roots of unity (Volume Conjecture [kashaev1997, murakami-murakami2001]). The Jones polynomial forms a Chern–Simons expectation value whose framing dependence produces the U(1) phase (Witten [witten1989], Reshetikhin–Turaev [reshetikhin1991]). The complexified continuation of the phase forms Witten [witten2011], and the bar-involution structure of the root-of-unity asymptotics forms the quantum-modularity of Zagier [zagier2010]. The quantum dilogarithm controlling the asymptotics forms Faddeev–Kashaev [faddeev1994].

Read against this work, two of the identifications constitute recombinations and two are specific to this framework. The reading modulus/argument = volume/Chern–Simons and the placement of the argument as a U(1) framing phase restate the cited results. The identification of the modulus with mass \lVert\mathrm{tr}_M\rVert and of color with the S_3\subset S_5 representation grading of the Bring quintic's Galois group are the paper's own. The literature offers the nearby A_5 / S_5 flavor and modular-flavor symmetries rather than this trace-algebra grading. The contribution forms the group-theoretic statement that these three readings are orthogonal sectors of one trace object, alongside the rigidity barring the continuous phase from being the discrete color charge.

Classical antecedents of the involutive reading

Resolving one object into observables under an involution is a recurring structure. Four classical instances frame the present one:

  • Frobenius–Schur indicator. The character involution \chi\mapsto\chi(g^{-1}) [frobenius-schur1906]—the bar-involution q\mapsto q^{-1} on the Hecke side—sorts every irreducible representation as real, quaternionic, or complex. The bar-even (binding, \cosh) and bar-odd (\beta-decay, \sinh) channels construct the rank-one shadow of this trichotomy on the trace.
  • Modular conjugation. The Markov trace forms a trace on a finite von Neumann algebra [jones1985]. Every such algebra carries the Tomita–Takesaki modular conjugation J and modular operator \Delta [takesaki1970]. The observable elements are the J-fixed (self-adjoint) ones, and a=\tfrac12(a+a^*)+\tfrac12(a-a^*) forms the algebra-level bar-parity split. The polar reading (mass =\lVert\mathrm{tr}_M\rVert, phase =\arg\mathrm{tr}_M) provides its modulus–modular-flow form.
  • Weil operator. On a polarized Hodge structure, the Weil operator [weil1958] supplies the complex structure packaging real harmonic periods into a polarized complex period. The complex volume \mathrm{Vol}+i\,\mathrm{CS} [neumann-zagier1985] provides such a period, and H^1(\mathrm{Bring})=2W forms such a structure—the Hodge-theoretic home of the complex-volume half.
  • Conjugate-variable amplitude. The oscillator amplitude a=q+ip combines a canonically conjugate pair through the symplectic complex structure, with \lVert a\rVert^2 the energy and \arg a the phase.

In physics, this reading follows the complex-energy / resonance tradition. A state forms a complex pole \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{pole}}=\mathfrak{m}-i\Gamma/2 (Gamow [gamow1928], Breit–Wigner [breit-wigner1936]) whose real part gives mass and whose imaginary part gives decay width. The bound sector lies on the conjugation-fixed real axis, and the optical theorem ties the imaginary part to the total decay rate. The Kramers–Kronig dispersion relations [kronig1926] lock the reactive (real) and absorptive (imaginary) parts of one causal response. There, the involution is complex conjugation / time reversal. Here, the bar-involution q\mapsto q^{-1} plays that role at the fibre level. One claims not the involutive reading itself, but its realization on the categorical knot trace, where \mathrm{Im}(q_0)=0 at the archimedean level renders the two parts separately real observable shadows.
rem:color-spacetime-s5-factorization-der:
Remark Single trace object, discreteness of the winding phase, and the Lean formalisation.

A single trace object

The embeddable strand counts dictate a single trace algebra H_2(q) \oplus H_3(q) carrying 2+3=5 irreducible representations (Cohomological embedding: torus knot representations exhaust H^1(\Sigma_g)). These match Bring's five homogeneous coordinates, partitioned into a rank-two spacetime block and a rank-three color block (brings-qou-4tuple). The color content of an embedded photon is recorded as an element of H_3(q), where the generators \sigma_0, \sigma_1 serve as the color axes (knot-basis-color-content). Color therefore provides a grading on the trace algebra itself, rather than a separate object.

The aether symmetry S_5 acts on all five coordinates. Its block-diagonal subgroup S_2 \times S_3 permutes spacetime and color separately. The S_3 permutes the three color sheets while preserving spacetime (color-sector-coords, Chirality and trefoil subgroups). The S_2 permutes the two spacetime coordinates while preserving color. Parts (1) and (2) make this precise. The product embeds faithfully, and each factor fixes the opposing sector pointwise. Color and spacetime function as independent coordinates on a single object. They couple only through S_5 elements outside S_2 \times S_3, which rotate spacetime indices into color indices.

Discreteness

Part (3) enforces rigidity on the continuous sector. The connected group \mathbb{R} is divisible, so any homomorphism to a finite group G vanishes. For each x, f(x) = f\big(|G| \cdot \tfrac{x}{|G|}\big) = |G| \cdot f(\tfrac{x}{|G|}) = 0, because |G| \cdot g = 0 for every g \in G. A continuous winding parameter cannot carry a finite-group (e.g. \mu_5) character. Physically, this dictates that the continuous trace phase does not constitute the discrete color charge (Mass is the modulus, electromagnetism the phase, color the S_3 grading of one trace).

Scope

The construction is generic. The embedding and divisibility arguments rely strictly on combinatorial data, requiring no archimedean input.

rem:u-coordinate-discharges:
Remark Macdonald coordinate u = q^2 discharges — closed-form rational identities replacing \mathtt{Real.sqrt}-laden scalar invariants (b^2 = (u^2+u+1)/(u+1)^2, \dim_q^2 V_{(2,1)} = u + 2 + u^{-1}, etc.). Macdonald coordinate u = q^2 substantive discharges for H_3 / V_{(2,1)} scalar invariants.

Many scalar invariants in the Hecke and Wenzl-bridge algebras are rational in the Macdonald coordinate u = q^2, even when their defining formulas involve square roots in q. This Macdonald substitution eliminates the square roots.

Substantive identities

See Table.

Because the substitution removes square roots, each identity reduces to an equality of rational functions in u, verified by clearing denominators, with no further input.

Significance

An explicit-residual discharge that only records that a residual evaluates to 0 is abstractly trivial: no concrete computation connects it to the underlying aether arithmetic. The u-coordinate identities express the underlying scalars as rational functions in a single variable u, so each equality becomes a mechanically checkable identity of rational functions.

For example, the Hecke quadratic relation for every generator of H_3(q) requires a residual to vanish. The substantive reason for this vanishing is the relation q \cdot (q - q^{-1}) = u - 1, a non-trivial rational identity.

Downstream dependencies

These u-coordinate identities act as the computational backing for several downstream blocks:
